proposals.before: After Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wanted to continue Wu with the son of Marquis De, and continue Chu with Prince Yuan's son Liu Li.
proposals.after: After Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wanted to continue Wu with the son of Marquis De, and continue Chu with Prince Yuan's son Li.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元王子禮 does not supply the surname Liu; the literal English invents Liu before Li.

proposals.before: King Zhao Liu Sui—his father was Gaozu's middle son, named You, posthumously titled "You."
proposals.after: King Zhao Liu Sui—his father was Gaozu's middle son, named You (友), posthumously titled You (幽, "the Secluded").
proposals.reason: Personal name 友 and posthumous name 幽 are different graphs both rendered You; the literal fails to distinguish them or convey 幽.

proposals.before: Empress Dowager Gao installed Lu Lu as King of Zhao, but within a year she passed away.
proposals.after: Empress Dowager Gao installed Lü Lu as King of Zhao, but within a year she passed away.
proposals.reason: Chinese 呂祿 uses the surname Lü; idiomatic Lu Lu drops the umlaut and obscures the Lü clan identity.

decisions.after: After Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wanted to continue Wu with the son of Marquis De, and continue Chu with King Yuan's son Liu Li.
decisions.reason: Although this unit abbreviates the name to 禮, the genealogy identifies King Yuan's son as Liu Li (劉禮); retaining the surname supports correct identity resolution.

decisions.after: King Zhao Liu Sui—his father was Gaozu's middle son, whose personal name was You and whose posthumous title was You, "the Secluded."
decisions.reason: The personal name You and posthumous title You represent different Chinese words; naming each category and translating the latter distinguishes them without inserting Chinese into the English field.
呂祿 is the Lü surname; idiomatic Lu Lu loses the umlaut and conflates it with unrelated Lu surnames, while Lü Lu matches the Chinese and the unit's own literal.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows English Lu Lu came only from the bad idiomatic of 呂祿; the personal-name claim must read Lü Lu while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
